To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

VitD treatment of PBMCs reduced the frequency of HIV-1 infected CD4+ cells and the number viral particles per infected cell, reduced the frequency of T cell activation, reduced production of granzymes and cytokines, and increased the expression of antiviral genes.

Treatment of peripheral blood mononu-clear cells (PBMC) with calcitrol reduced the susceptibility of CD4 T cells to HIV infection in vitro, by modulating the activation and function levels of T cells and by increasing the transcriptional expression levels of antiviral genes.
Vitamin D treatment of PBMCs modulated immune activation of T cells and reduced susceptibility to X4- and to R5-tropic strains HIV-1 infection in CD4+ T-cells from Co-HC, but not in those from HESNs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of vitamin D (Vit D) in HIV-1 infection and its potential use in the prevention of HIV-1 transmission.
the role that the immune response plays in HIV-1 infection and its implications in the pathogenesis of AIDS.
the role of Vitamin D in the modulation of immune activation and HIV-1 susceptibility of T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment of PBMCs with calcitriols reduced the susceptibility of CD4 cells to HIV- infection, but only in Co-HC.
the effect of VitD in HIV infection and transmission is not straightforward and depends on several factors such as the type of HIV-1 strain and the host genetic and immune status.

the in vitro treatment of PBMCs from HIV unexposed donors with the active form VitD (calcitriol) reduces the susceptibility of CD4 T cells to infection by HIV-1 strains with different tropism, by modulating T cell function and activation, and the expression of antiviral genes, and that these effects were more pronounced in Co-HC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VitD treatment of PBMCs modulates immune activation and function and reduced susceptibility to X4- and to a lesser extend to R5- HIV-1 infection.
VitD may have a role in the modulation of HIV-1 susceptibility, and therefore could be used to prevent HIV- 1 infection.
calcitriol could reduce HIV- 1 infection by reducing immune activation, increasing the expression of antiviral genes and by decreasing the production of inflammatory factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the active form of Vitamin D, calcitrirol, reduces HIV-1 infection in CD4+ T cell from healthy individuals, but not from HESNs, through the modulation of T cells activation, and the expression of antiviral genes.
VitD could reduce HIV- 1 transmission, through a specific modulation on the activation levels and functions of T cells, in addition to the production of antiretroviral factors.
calcitriol can reduce the frequency of HIV-1-infected cells and viral particles per cell by modulating the function of T cells.
